messages.subject: Work Group tomorrow: 10-noon
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

This is your weekly reminder of tomorrow's R Users Group work group. As usual, it will be held from 10-noon at the data lab classroom and on zoom. If you're attending virtually, please post your questions to the discourse site ahead of time. Info+links below.

Best,
Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators

________________________________________________________________
This quarter we'll be meeting from 10-noon on Wednesdays (same as last fall). In light of the recent move to in-person classes, we will be meeting in a hybrid format, via zoom <https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/92807937862>, and in the Data Lab classroom (360 Shields Library).

Please remember to post your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

For those not familiar with D-RUG, the R Users' Group is a weekly working group to get some help with R-specific coding problems. The coordinators are various and sundry coding connoisseurs, ranging from UCD data scientists to grad students on campus. We meet for 2 hours in an open-forum format, so you can treat D-RUG as a communal, co-working environment: come hang out and chat, work on your own, seek help, make friends. Or, a little bit of everything! Check out our website <https://d-rug.github.io/> for more information.

We are also seeking presenters! It is nice to mix things up with occasional presentations. In the past, we've had (15- to 45-minute) presentations ranging from data types, to tidyverse tools, to spatial data, to the Google Earth Engine plugin for R. If you would like to hone your teaching, need an excuse to perfect your cRaft, or want to show off a cool R trick you learned, shoot us an email and we can add your presentation to our calendar <https://d-rug.github.io/calendar.html>! Presentations can be in-person or virtual (and in-person presentations will be streamed for virtual attendees).
--
Christian John — Ph.D. candidate
NASA FINESST Future Investigator
Pronouns: he/him/his

Google Scholar <https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=VPd60tMAAAAJ&view_op=list_works&authuser=1&sortby=pubdate>

short-term job opportunity for geospatial R folks...

“The good life of any river may depend on the perception of its music; and the preservation of some music to perceive.”

― Aldo Leopold

Ryan Peek, PhD (he/him)
Aquatic Ecologist, Post-Doctoral Researcher
Center for Watershed Sciences, UC Davis
ryanpeek.org <https://ryanpeek.org/>
@riverpeek
530.754.5351

-----------------------------------------------------

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Jamie Hansen-Lewis <jhanse...@ucdavis.edu>
Date: Wed, Apr 6, 2022 at 5:08 PM
Subject: [geospatial] geospatial data visualization job
To: <geosp...@ucdavis.edu>

I'm hiring for a short-term job creating figures of geospatial data. The work requires using R or python to write scripts that create maps of a number of polygon, raster, and point datasets for academic publication. Input on the data visualization aesthetics would be appreciated.

As a starting point, the job is roughly 20-30 hours at $35 an hour over the next 2-3 weeks. I'm seeking a fast turnaround. If interested, please reply in an email to me (jhanse...@ucdavis.edu) with a CV/resume, availability, and a pdf of some map you've made with R or python.

Thanks, j

_
Jamie Hansen-Lewis
Assistant Professor
Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics
University of California, Davis

messages.subject: #maptimeDavis Workshop: Working with Cal-Adapt Climate Data in R (#maptimeDavis & D-RUG)
messages.subject_clean: #maptimeDavis Workshop: Working with Cal-Adapt Climate Data in R (#maptimeDavis & D-RUG)
messages.body_plain:
Hi all! #maptimeDavis and Davis R Users Group are having a workshop on Tuesday featuring UC  ANR’s Andy Lyons! Please join us!  (Also, I recommend you register well before the event so the system has time to send you the Zoom link before the workshop starts.)

Working with Cal-Adapt Climate Data in R (#maptimeDavis & D-RUG)
April 26 @ 10:00 am -  12:00 pm

Description

Cal-Adapt is California’s official go-to source for downscaled climate data. Most people interact with Cal-Adapt through the website, but Cal-Adapt also features an API which can be used to query and import data through programming languages.

This hands-on workshop will teach you how to work with climate data wisely using caladaptR (https://ucanr-igis.github.io/caladaptr/), a R package which streamlines the process of importing data via the Cal-Adapt API. Through short hands-on exercises, you will learn how to construct API requests, fetch data from Cal-Adapt as data frames and rasters, and wrangle the data for analysis and visualization. Examples will showcase techniques for aggregating climate projections from multiple climate models and years, joining modeled climate data to other tabular data, transforming climate projections into more intuitive probabilities, and visualization through plots and maps. Data wrangling, analysis, and mapping examples will use the tidyverse, sf, tmap, and stars packages.

Learning Objectives

Participants in this workshop will
Learn how to construct API requests and fetch climate data from Cal-Adapt
Understand best practices for working with climate data wisely
Understand techniques for converting climate data into actionable info

Prerequisites

This hands-on portions of the workshop will be in R. Basic familiarity with R and RStudio (at least enough to run the sample code provided) is suggested.

Familiarity with climate data is helpful but not required. A short primer on climate data will be provided.

Software:

R and R studio

For more suggested preparation, see:  https://ucanr-igis.github.io/caladaptr-res/workshops/ca_intro_feb22/setup.html

A free RStudio Cloud account is strongly encouraged

Instructor: Andy Lyons, UC ANR

Instructor Bio

Andy Lyons is Program Coordinator for the Informatics and GIS Statewide Program in the UC Division of Agriculture and Natural Resources. His R projects include packages to analyze animal movement, manage drone imagery, import climate data, and decision support tools for tree crops. He holds a PhD in Environmental Science Policy and Management from UC Berkeley.

Location: Zoom. Click link below to register for this workshop.

Register:  https://registration.genomecenter.ucdavis.edu/events/cal-adapt-spring2022/

Cost: Free of charge.

Whenever possible, #maptimeDavis Workshops will be recorded and posted on the DataLab YouTube channel <https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCTooXK1RiSHNbWsmeqz0W6g>. #maptimeDavis Studio will not be recorded to encourage open discussion. Weekly reminders will be sent on the Geospatial Email List <https://lists.ucdavis.edu/sympa/info/geospatial>.

#maptimeDavis Workshops and Studio are a product of UC Davis DataLab’s Spatial Sciences Research Cluster <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/spatial-sciences/> and are supported by the contributions and participation of our community. Please send questions to Michele Tobias mmto...@ucdavis.edu
